title: Inverse Coin Change
summary: Given a 1-indexed integer array numWays, where numWays[i] indicates the number of ways to achieve a total amount of i using an infinite supply of some fixed coin denominations, your task is to determine the unique coin denominations that could have produced this array.
statement: Given a 1-indexed integer array numWays, where numWays[i] indicates the number of ways to achieve a total amount of i using an infinite supply of some fixed coin denominations, your task is to determine the unique coin denominations that could have produced this array. Return a sorted array containing these denominations. If no such set of denominations exists, return an empty array.
constraints: numWays has length at most 100 and gives unordered infinite-coin combination counts for amounts one through n.
Denominations are unique positive integers at most n.
Return the unique sorted denomination set, or an empty list when the counts are inconsistent.
reference_solution:
def recover_coin_denominations(numWays):
    n=len(numWays);ways=[1]+[0]*n;coins=[]
    for amount in range(1,n+1):
        if ways[amount]==numWays[amount-1]:continue
        if ways[amount]+1!=numWays[amount-1]:return []
        coins.append(amount)
        for total in range(amount,n+1):ways[total]+=ways[total-amount]
    return coins if ways[1:]==numWays else []

hints: At amount d, larger coins cannot contribute and adding coin d creates exactly one new combination: the coin alone.
Reconstruct denominations from small to large while maintaining the forward coin-change DP produced so far.
If current ways equals target, skip d; if it is exactly one smaller, add d and update ascending totals; otherwise reject.
Induction fixes every denomination uniquely because all smaller choices are already known and no larger denomination affects the current amount.
